newsitem.title: UK: Labour confident on eve of key British by-election.
newsitem.headline: Labour confident on eve of key British by-election.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party wrapped up campaigning on Wednesday for the key Wirral South by-election confident it can capture the seat and get a flying start for the coming general election.

The ruling Conservatives, who would become a minority in parliament if they lose Wirral South on Thursday, said they were fighting to win but acknowledged that by-elections often go against the government of the day.
"Tonight we stand on the verge of a historic threshold," Labour's foreign affairs spokesman, Robin Cook, said in remarks prepared for an eve-of-poll rally in the northwest England constituency.
"Tomorrow the electors of Wirral are going to lead Britain across it. A Labour win in Wirral will show Britain the way to the future."
Cook said Labour, which polls tip to win Wirral South, would capture the hitherto safe Conservative seat because it had offered a positive message.

"The voice of the Wirral this week will echo across Britain. It will be a blast that will bring down a tottering Tory government and will bring in a Labour government that looks to the future, not the past," he said.
Leading Conservatives have been at pains to dampen expectations, stressing that by-elections are traditionally an opportunity for voters to lodge a protest vote.
"There is always a by-election syndrome, but we are fighting to win," Education Secretary Gillian Shephard told a news conference at Conservative Central Office.
